published_by: The Insolvency Service, 'Individual insolvencies' monthly official statistics, Long-Run Series in CSV Format
what_this_is: THE PUBLISHED COUNT, NOT A READING OF IT. Breathing Space (Debt Respite Scheme) registrations in England and Wales, all creditors, summed here from the publisher's monthly NSA columns `EW_standard_breathing_space_NSA` and `EW_mental_health_breathing_space_NSA` into calendar years. A partial year is stored PARTIAL, with the period it covers; annualising it is a reading and is done by the reader (simulation/debt_respite_draw.py) and re-done independently by the year-keyed rate census, never here. Nothing here says how many registrations name an energy creditor: no publisher splits by creditor type (see debt_respite_breathing_space_moratorium.json, NOT_ESTABLISHED).

basis.units: registrations (moratoria entered on the register), a count per person, NSA
basis.territory: England and Wales only (SI 2020/1311 reg 1(8)-(9)); the scheme does not run in Scotland or NI
basis.partial_years: 2021 runs from the scheme's start on 2021-05-04; the latest year runs to the last month in the edition. `months_reported` and the period dates are the publisher's coverage, stated so the reader can annualise without guessing.

provenance_legend.primary: summed on 2026-11-18 from the October 2026 edition's long-run CSV (sha256 36dd6e9a20a6d988387395ebf6681aac2c75312714faa5c6d99e18f8991fa105). The August 2026 edition (sha256 9ea95adde33ac10152e99ac1347b38d75a84055fe1f3045270e973c999f6954d), which docs/market_research/debt_and_collections.md and the first build of the world's draw read, was fetched the same day: its 2021-2025 sums are identical to October's, so the only movement between editions is the 2026 year-to-date running from 8 to 10 months.

r13_wall: Published counts, transcribed blind to company results. No value here may be moved because a moratorium rate in a run looks wrong.
portability: One E&W scheme. Scotland's moratorium on diligence is a different instrument with its own (Accountant in Bankruptcy) statistics and would be its own artefact.

source_check.publication: The Insolvency Service, Individual insolvencies, October 2026 (published 2026-11-17): 'Long-Run Series in CSV Format - Individual Insolvency Statistics October 2026'.
source_check.how_to_recheck: A NEW EDITION IS A NEW PAGE, monthly, so the stored URL never moves: GET https://www.gov.uk/api/content/government/collections/individual-insolvency-statistics-releases and read `links.documents` -- a release whose `public_updated_at` is later than `version_token` is a newer edition. Take its long-run CSV from that release's `details.attachments` (content_type text/csv, title beginning 'Long-Run Series'); the asset URL is a hash and must not be stored as the key. Re-sum the two breathing-space NSA columns by `year` and compare: a revision to a closed year is a supersession, an extra month in the open year is expected.

checked_for_supersession.note: October 2026 is the latest release in the collection on this date.
